name: SK9822 addressable RGB LED strip (60 LEDs, 1 m)
description: Strip of 60 individually addressable SK9822 RGB LEDs (Opsco, APA102-compatible two-wire clock + data SPI, up to 30 MHz, 8-bit PWM per colour plus a 5-bit constant-current brightness). Runs on 5 V (datasheet 4.5-5.3 V); about 50 mA per LED at full white, so up to 3 A for the metre: it needs its own 5 V supply. Sold as: Pololu Addressable RGB 60-LED Strip, 5V, 1m (SK9822), item #3089 (4-pin JST SM input lead: black GND, green DI, yellow CI, red VCC; strip pads VCC, CI, DI, GND).
eli5: A metre of 60 colour lights you set one by one with a clock wire and a data wire. It is easy to drive because there is no tricky timing.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (black wire). Join it to the microcontroller's GND and the 5 V supply's GND.

pins.name: DI
pins.description: Data in (green wire), sampled on the rising edge of CI. Input only; 3.3 V logic usually works, a 74AHCT125 makes it reliable.

pins.name: CI
pins.description: Clock in (yellow wire), idles low, up to 30 MHz. Input only.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: LED supply (red wire), 5 V (4.5-5.3 V). Up to about 3 A at full white for 60 LEDs: use a separate 5 V supply.

buildNotes: Use the INPUT end of the strip (pads labelled DI and CI, arrow pointing away). The JST SM input lead is black GND, green DI, yellow CI, red VCC; the output end (DO, CO) only chains to another strip.
Power the strip from a separate 5 V supply rated for at least 3 A (60 LEDs x 50 mA at full white) and join its GND to the microcontroller's GND. Never feed more than 5.3 V.

Send a 32-zero-bit start frame, 4 bytes per LED (0xE0 | brightness, blue, green, red), then a 32-zero-bit reset frame and at least n/2 more zero clocks. The SK9822 shows new colours only when that reset/start frame arrives; ones as the end frame can glitch the first LED.
The SK9822 datasheet gives no input-high threshold: 3.3 V signals usually work on short wires, but add a 74AHCT125 level shifter powered from 5 V if the strip flickers.
Put a 1000 uF capacitor across VCC and GND at the strip input. Pololu recommends a separate supply feed every 180 LEDs.

driver.code:
# SK9822 addressable RGB LED strip (APA102-compatible two-wire SPI), MicroPython driver.
# Frame format from the SK9822 datasheet (Opsco, rev 01, section 9):
#   start frame : 32 zero bits
#   LED frame   : 0b111 + 5-bit global brightness, then BLUE, GREEN, RED (8 bits each, MSB first)
# The datasheet shows an end frame of 32 one bits, but the SK9822 (unlike the APA102) only
# moves the new colours to its outputs when it sees the NEXT start frame, and ones after the
# data can be taken as an extra LED frame. So, as Pololu and cpldcpu recommend, we send a
# 32-zero-bit "reset frame" after the LED data (latches this update) and then at least n/2
# more zero clock edges so the data reaches the last LED (each LED delays it by half a clock).
#
# Clock idles low and data is sampled on the rising edge: SPI mode 0 (polarity=0, phase=0).
# The datasheet allows up to 30 MHz; long wires and 3.3 V logic are happier at 1-4 MHz.
#
# brightness (0-31) sets the drive current of all three LEDs in each pixel (n/31 of 20 mA
# max), the 8-bit colour values set the PWM duty (n/256). Each pixel draws about 50 mA at
# full white with brightness 31.


class SK9822:
    def __init__(self, spi, n, brightness=4):
        self.spi = spi
        self.n = n
        self.brightness = brightness & 0x1F
        self.buf = [(0, 0, 0)] * n

    def __len__(self):
        return self.n

    def __setitem__(self, i, color):
        r, g, b = color
        self.buf[i] = (r & 0xFF, g & 0xFF, b & 0xFF)

    def __getitem__(self, i):
        return self.buf[i]

    def fill(self, color):
        r, g, b = color
        self.buf = [(r & 0xFF, g & 0xFF, b & 0xFF)] * self.n

    def set_brightness(self, level):
        """Global brightness 0-31 (drive current level/31)."""
        self.brightness = max(0, min(31, int(level)))

    def show(self):
        n = self.n
        out = bytearray(4 + 4 * n + 4 + (n + 15) // 16)  # all zeros
        hdr = 0xE0 | self.brightness
        k = 4
        for r, g, b in self.buf:
            out[k] = hdr
            out[k + 1] = b
            out[k + 2] = g
            out[k + 3] = r
            k += 4
        # out[k:] stays zero: 4-byte reset frame + end frame of n/2 clock edges.
        self.spi.write(out)

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import time
from sk9822 import SK9822

spi = SPI(1, baudrate=2000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({CI}), mosi=Pin({DI}))
strip = SK9822(spi, 60, brightness=8)
strip.fill((0, 0, 0))
strip.show()
time.sleep(1)
for i in range(60):
    strip[i] = (255, 0, 0) if i % 2 == 0 else (0, 0, 255)
strip.show()
print('strip lit: red/blue')
time.sleep(1.5)
strip.fill((0, 0, 0))
strip.show()
print('strip off')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: The strip starts dark, lights red/blue, then goes dark again
